headline: Anthropic makes its Nasdaq debut today as crypto platforms offer tokens that track its shares, while bitcoin trades near its lowest since July as fear stays extreme and Fed rate-rise worries weigh.

market.asOf: Read at about 07:55-08:00 UTC Thu 19 Nov (about 15:00 Bangkok). BTC and SOL from CoinGecko's coin pages, ETH from CoinMarketCap's Ethereum page because CoinGecko's would not load. Pages on both sites showed conflicting prices (BTC between about $62,600 and $63,600), so treat these as rough. The 24-hour moves disagreed and are left out. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: alternative.me's Crypto Fear & Greed Index 11 (12 yesterday, 29 a week ago, 59 a month ago); CoinMarketCap's own Fear & Greed Index also 11. Both read at about 08:00 UTC Thu 19 Nov.

stories.title: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq today, and crypto platforms launch tokens that track its shares
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic priced its shares at $83, above its $70-78 range, and starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday. It is the biggest IPO on record. Crypto platforms including Ondo and Binance Wallet are offering tokens that track the share price. These tokens do not make you a shareholder, and many are not open to US residents.
points: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83, raising about $81.3 billion at a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, per Yahoo Finance; Reuters, via Investing.com, calls it the biggest IPO on record.
The first trade may come after the 9:30am ET open: new listings start in Nasdaq's IPO Cross once the lead bank is ready, per Stocktitan.
Ondo is launching a token tracking ANT for eligible investors outside the US only; holders get price exposure but do not own the stock, per The Block.
Kraken's page says its tokenized IPO access is not open to US clients, who can buy ANT as a regular stock from its first trading day.
Binance Wallet's sale had a 500 million USDC cap; its tokens are issued by Backed, are not Anthropic stock and carry no voting or dividend rights, per Bitcoin.com.

sources.label: Stocktitan: how the first trade works

stories.title: Bitcoin falls to its lowest since July as Fed rate-rise fears grow and fund outflows continue
stories.summary: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed nearly all officials expect to raise rates in December, and Governor Waller said a bigger half-point rise should be considered. Bitcoin touched its lowest level since July early Thursday, and money kept leaving US bitcoin funds on Wednesday.
points: Nearly all Fed officials expect a quarter-point rise in December, and Waller backed a half point, per AP via KSAT; CME FedWatch was near 95% for a December rise.
Waller said inflation is 'headed in the wrong direction', per Investing.com via Yahoo Finance.
Bitcoin hit its lowest level since July in early Thursday trading, with an intraday low of about $62,399.50, per Investing.com via Yahoo Finance.
US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $306.5 million on Wednesday 18 Nov, with no fund taking in money; spot ether funds lost $39.8 million, per Farside data reported by KuCoin.
CryptoQuant says bitcoin is below its 200-day average of about $72,900 and sees $62,000-65,000 as a possible support range, per The Block.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: bitcoin lowest since July

stories.title: Ledger finds tampered hardware wallets sold in Berlin and Dubai
stories.summary: Ledger widened its investigation into tampered hardware wallets to Germany and the UAE. Attackers bought real devices, added hardware that leaks the recovery phrase during setup, and sent them back into reseller channels. Ledger says its chip and software are not flawed and no device bought on ledger.com is affected. The lesson: buy hardware wallets from the maker and never use a recovery phrase you did not create.
points: Two tampered units were reported in Dubai and 'a few' in Berlin; Ledger asks anyone who bought a device in Berlin since January to contact support, per The Block.
Two X users report about $604,000 lost combined from devices bought from an authorized Dubai reseller; Ledger has not confirmed loss figures, per The Block.
Bitquery estimates about $1.68 million taken from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, after about $102 million from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia earlier, per The Block.
Ledger says there is 'no flaw in Ledger's secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com', per The Block.

sources.label: The Block: Ledger incidents in Germany and UAE

briefs.title: Binance wins $6.5B freezing order over October hack
briefs.summary: An Abu Dhabi court granted a worldwide freezing order; Binance says about $2.85 billion of about $6.34 billion in affected assets has been frozen or intercepted, per The Block.

briefs.title: Coinbase blocks $4.7M headed to a deepfake giveaway
briefs.summary: Coinbase's AI defenses stopped about $4.7 million going to scammers running a fake Elon Musk giveaway livestream, per The Block.

briefs.title: World Bank tests USDC payouts
briefs.summary: The World Bank Group is testing USDC with Circle and Citi for disbursements, per The Block.

briefs.title: Variational raises $110M
briefs.summary: The onchain derivatives platform raised a $110 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Bain Capital Crypto, per The Block.

briefs.title: Strategy buys 485 more bitcoin
briefs.summary: Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4 million over 9-15 Nov, bringing its holdings to 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452, per its SEC filing.

briefs.title: Kraken's parent agrees to buy Tribe Capital
briefs.summary: Payward is acquiring Tribe Capital to expand its private-market offerings, per The Block.

calendar.event: Anthropic's first day of trading on Nasdaq as ANT
calendar.note: Priced at $83, per Yahoo Finance. The market opens at 9:30am ET, but a new listing's first trade comes in Nasdaq's IPO Cross once the lead bank is ready, which can be hours after the open, per Stocktitan.

SEC nominees Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine appear before the Senate Banking Committee with other nominees, per the committee's page. Fed's Goolsbee (12:30pm ET), Barkin (4:00pm ET) and Paulson (6:30pm ET) speak, per TD Economics, and Barr at 2:15pm ET, per the Fed.

calendar.note: Forecast 52, per Finviz; the preliminary November reading was 51.0, per StockAnalysis, and October's final was 48.0, per Finviz. Fed's Waller speaks at 8:25am ET and Cook at 12:15pm ET (00:15 Sat Bangkok), per the Fed.
Prior 91.7, per Finviz; no forecast published there. Dell, Workday and HP report after the US close, per IfYouSpent.
